title: RESONANCE
author: Andries J. Greyling
rationale: Near-future South Africa, KwaZulu-Natal mining country. Afrikaans applies (SA setting). isiZulu is the book's African-language core. Spanish + French are the catalog-wide market languages. NOT a full eleven-official-language sweep: the book's own canon says 'Do NOT translate every isiZulu phrase' and centres on KZN/Zulu — a mechanical 11-language treatment would betray its design.

targets.name: Afrikaans
directives: Afrikaans is itself a character-language in this book (boardroom/mine code-switching). When the SOURCE already has an Afrikaans word (veld, stoep, rooibos), leave it — do not 're-translate' it into a different Afrikaans register.

isiZulu passages that are untranslated in the source STAY untranslated and unchanged — do not render them into Afrikaans. They read as isiZulu to an Afrikaans reader exactly as they do to an English one.
Voice: natural, contemporary South African Afrikaans (Standaardafrikaans with lived warmth), not Netherlands Dutch and not archaic Bybel-Afrikaans.
Keep the honey-badger / pangolin imagery literal (ratel, ietermagog) — these animals are native and the words exist.

targets.name: isiZulu
directives: This makes the book's HOME language its whole-text language. The isiZulu phrases already in the source are now simply part of the prose — keep them, and let the surrounding translated text meet them seamlessly.

Technical / robotics / mining-equipment terms may stay in English where a natural isiZulu speaker would code-switch to English (the source itself does this) — do not invent neologisms for 'exoskeleton', 'neural interface', etc.
Proverb 'Umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu' is load-bearing; keep it verbatim and do NOT also gloss it — the isiZulu reader needs no gloss.
Voice: standard isiZulu as written in KwaZulu-Natal; respectful registers (sawubona/sanibona, isiHlonipho where the scene calls for it).

targets.name: Spanish
directives: Neutral/international Spanish (español neutro) for the widest readership — avoid region-locked slang.

ALL South African words — isiZulu terms AND the cultural flavour words (veld, biltong, rooibos, stoep, mealie) — stay verbatim and italicised as foreign terms, exactly as they are foreign in the English source. Do not Hispanicise them and do not add footnotes the source lacks.
Preserve the code-switching texture: where the English narration brushes against isiZulu, the Spanish narration does the same — the foreignness is the point.
Invented entities (Guardian, SAGE, the Court, IAOC) keep their English names.

targets.name: French
directives: Same foreign-term rule as Spanish: South African words (isiZulu + veld/biltong/rooibos/stoep/mealie) stay verbatim, italicised, unglossed.
Invented entities keep their English names (Guardian, SAGE, the Court, IAOC).
Respect register shifts: the mine floor and the IAOC boardroom are different Frenches.

global_directives: PRESERVE the front-matter structure of build/BOOK.md exactly: title block, copyright page, dedication, epigraphs, chapter order, and any back matter (glossary, acknowledgements). Translate their CONTENT; keep their ORDER and markdown structure byte-for-byte where it's structural (headings, '---' rules, '⁂' breaks).
The copyright notice, ISBN line, and 'Published by the House of Greyling' stay — translate surrounding prose but keep proper nouns and the legal sense intact.
Do NOT add translator's notes, footnotes, or bracketed glosses that the English source does not contain. The source trusts the reader; so does every edition.
Chapter titles ARE translated (e.g. 'The Wire Push Car') unless they are proper nouns.
Output one file per language at build/BOOK.<code>.md, ready for tools/render_book.sh.
